briefs.title: Census Bureau page describes Advance Economic Indicators report on goods trade and inventories
briefs.summary: The US Census Bureau's Advance Economic Indicators page says the report provides advance statistics for U.S. international trade in goods, domestic retail inventories and domestic wholesale inventories. It says goods trade data are compiled by commodity classification, quantities, values, shipping weights, transport method, state of origin, customs district and port, destination country, and whether goods are domestic or re-exports. The retrieved text is a program description and contains no figures from the latest release. It also notes that FRED now incorporates the Census Bureau's 13 economic indicators.

briefs.title: Renta 4 research head sees Colombia's fiscal credibility at risk without concrete cuts
briefs.summary: Rafael Molina, director of Research at Renta 4 Global Fiduciaria, told Valora Analitik that delays in issuing decrees and effective budget cuts have created skepticism among investors. He projects inflation closing this year at 6.8% and ending 2027 between 5.5% and 5.6%, and says Banco de la República could raise rates by 25 basis points at its December meeting. He cites a 2027 deficit that could approach 9.4% without reform and gives his own estimate of about 8.5%. He does not see an imminent default risk in the next year and says an IMF agreement could act as a relief valve.

es.title: Renta 4: la credibilidad fiscal de Colombia está en riesgo sin recortes concretos
es.summary: Rafael Molina, director de Research de Renta 4 Global Fiduciaria, dijo a Valora Analitik que la demora en decretos y recortes presupuestales efectivos ha generado escepticismo entre los inversionistas. Proyecta que la inflación cierre este año en 6,8 % y que en 2027 se ubique entre 5,5 % y 5,6 %, y señala que el Banco de la República podría subir las tasas 25 puntos básicos en su reunión de diciembre. Cita un déficit para 2027 que podría rozar el 9,4 % sin reforma y da una estimación propia cercana al 8,5 %. No ve un riesgo de default inminente en el próximo año y dice que un acuerdo con el FMI podría ser una válvula de escape.

briefs.title: EIA: global electricity generation reached 31.8 trillion kWh in 2025, over double 2000

source.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (Today in Energy)

briefs.summary: The EIA reports that the world generated 31.8 trillion kWh of electricity in 2025, versus 15.1 trillion kWh in 2000. Renewables rose from 2.9 trillion kWh to 10.6 trillion kWh, a 34% share of the 2025 mix, and surpassed coal, whose share fell from a 41% peak in 2007 to 33%. China, the United States and India together generated 17.3 trillion kWh in 2025, more than the rest of the world combined. China generated 10.7 trillion kWh, the US 4.5 trillion kWh and India 2.1 trillion kWh.

actors.reason: Renewable generation grew from 2.9 to 10.6 trillion kWh between 2000 and 2025 and became the largest source in 2025, according to the EIA.

actors.reason: Coal output grew 83% from 2000 to 2024, but its share of world generation fell from 41% in 2007 to 33% in 2025.

actors.reason: US generation growth averaged 2% a year in 2020-2025, much of it from commercial demand including data centers, per the EIA.

actors.name: India's power system
actors.reason: Generation more than tripled since 2000 and 70% of the 2025 output came from coal, so demand growth is tied largely to coal.

briefs.title: BanRep's Acosta says 2027 minimum wage rise should be around 8%
briefs.summary: In an interview with Bloomberg Línea, as reported by Valora Analitik, Banco de la República co-director Olga Lucía Acosta said the 2027 minimum wage increase should be around 8%. She based this on inflation closing 2026 at 7% at most and labor productivity growth near 1%. She said the 23% rise set for 2026 was followed by weaker formal employment in labor-intensive sectors, and that the central bank expects 2027 growth slightly below 2%. She also said conditions for gradual rate cuts could emerge in the second half of 2027 if fiscal and monetary policy align.

es.title: Codirectora del BanRep, Acosta, plantea que el mínimo de 2027 suba cerca de 8 %
es.summary: En una entrevista con Bloomberg Línea, reportada por Valora Analitik, la codirectora del Banco de la República, Olga Lucía Acosta, dijo que el aumento del salario mínimo para 2027 debería ubicarse en torno al 8 %. Se basó en una inflación que cerraría 2026 «a lo sumo en 7 %» y un avance de la productividad laboral cercano al 1 %. Afirmó que tras el alza de 23 % fijada para 2026 se deterioró el empleo formal en sectores intensivos en mano de obra, y que el banco prevé un crecimiento ligeramente inferior a 2 % en 2027. Añadió que en el segundo semestre de 2027 podrían darse las condiciones para una reducción gradual de las tasas si la política fiscal y la monetaria se armonizan.

briefs.title: Asian and European stocks rise as AI shares rebound; Brent up 1.1% to US$97.66
briefs.summary: Most Asian markets rose on Friday, with China's CSI 300 up 3.5% and South Korea's Kospi up 4.1%, after China's State Council pledged more capital-market support and AI-related tech stocks recovered. The Stoxx 600 was up 0.9% in the morning session but was still on course for a 1.5% monthly decline in November, while European bond yields rose after ECB minutes with a hawkish tone. Brent futures rose 1.1% to US$97.66 and WTI gained 2.7% to US$85.97, as reported attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping near the Strait of Hormuz fueled supply concerns. Spot gold rose 3% to US$3,672.19. Tokyo core inflation reached 2.9% in November, up from 2.6% in October.

audit.title: Census Bureau page describes Advance Economic Indicators report on goods trade and inventories
Renta 4 research head sees Colombia's fiscal credibility at risk without concrete cuts

issues: Actor 'Colombian fixed income and peso investors' is marked 'adverse', but the source does not support an adverse impact for peso investors. Molina calls the peso 'high beta', reacting strongly to both good and bad news. He also says it strengthened after the move to $4,500 and projects it could stabilize at $3,250–3,300 before rising toward $3,450 in 2027. Only the fixed income and risk-premium pressure is supported as adverse. Split the actor or limit it to fixed income, and fix the reason in both EN and ES.

Actor 'Colombian oil industry' is marked 'mixed', but the source only states what Molina says the tax reform needs (RUGE incentives) and that tax burdens near 50% make investment hard to attract. It describes no actual mixed impact. 'undetermined', or an adverse reason tied explicitly to the current tax burden, would match the source better.

Deficit figures: the source is internally inconsistent, saying both the 9.4% and the 8.5% figures are 'sin reforma'. The draft's 'his own estimate of about 8.5%' drops that qualifier. Consider noting the ambiguity rather than implying a clean contrast.

IMF: the source says the negotiation with the IMF is an 'importante válvula de escape' and could facilitate an agreement with more flexible terms. The draft attributes the relief-valve role to 'an IMF agreement' in both EN and ES. This is a minor shift that should be aligned with the source wording.
Category 'Other' seems inappropriate for a fiscal, monetary policy and FX brief; a macro/economy category would fit better.

Summary omits Molina's rate path (short-term rates unlikely below 11% before mid-next year, long-term around 12.5%) and his FX projections. This is not an accuracy error, but it is relevant context for the peso actor.

audit.title: EIA: global electricity generation reached 31.8 trillion kWh in 2025, over double 2000

issues: Actor 'India's power system' (EN and ES): the reason says 'so demand growth is tied largely to coal' / 'el crecimiento de la demanda depende en gran medida de este'. The source does not say this. It reports that 70% of India's 2025 generation came from coal, which describes the generation mix, not what drives demand growth. The source attributes India's demand growth to population growth and a fast-growing manufacturing sector. Remove the inference, or restate it as the source does (e.g., 'generation more than tripled since 2000, averaging 5% a year, and 70% of 2025 output came from coal').
